chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Hamza ibn Abdullah al-Ja'fari from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Hamza al-Thumali. He said:
al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) said: Hope in Allah with a hope that does not entice you to sin against Him, and fear Allah with a fear that does not deprive you of His mercy.

key_terms.خوف: Fear, awe -- reverential fear of Allah's displeasure and punishment
key_terms.رجاء: Hope, expectation -- specifically hope in Allah's mercy and forgiveness
key_terms.رحمة: Mercy, compassion -- divine mercy that encompasses all creation
key_terms.معاصي: Acts of disobedience, sins -- violations of Allah's commands

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the balance between hope and fear in relation to Allah?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches the delicate balance between hope and fear in one's relationship with Allah. A believer should hope in Allah's mercy without letting that hope embolden them to commit sins, and should fear Allah without letting that fear drive them to despair of His mercy. This encapsulates a core Islamic spiritual principle: maintaining a middle path between complacency and hopelessness.
